clue.text: Ensured distribution to ultimate recipient

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters of the clue's first word are shared out in a new order

explanation.surface: A delivery firm promises a parcel reached the person it was meant for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution to' reads as delivery jargon; 'distribution' is the anagram signal working on 'Ensured'.
explanation.definitionFit: The final consumer of a product, the person it is ultimately delivered to and used by, is its end user.

clue.text: Salad dressing envied

indicators.note: dressing a dish means arranging it, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A salad dressing that someone covets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad dressing' looks like one phrase, but 'Salad' is the definition and 'dressing' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy chicory plant eaten raw in salads; the clue names the dish for the leaf by example.

clue.text: Quite possible for party to fit

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
fit, as in fit to do something, means able

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether there is room to squeeze in at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be done or achieved is feasible, entirely within reach.

clue.text: Downloads a new source for perfumery

indicators.note: new letters are made from the old words, rearranging them into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone downloads a fresh supplier list for a perfume business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on DOWNLOADS plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant heartwood of an Indian tree yields an oil much used in perfumes and incense.

clue.text: Endless dressing-up is now sure to be on the cards again

definitions.text: is now sure to be on the cards again

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word supplied is cut off

parts.note: robing is putting on ceremonial robes, a dressing-up

explanation.surface: A season of costume parties is surely coming round once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the red-breasted bird appears on Christmas cards, so with Christmas coming it will be 'on the cards' again. 'Endless' drops the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: This small red-breasted bird is a staple image of British Christmas cards each December.

clue.text: Jump on ice to enable first return to pool

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of enable is wanted
return means the word pool is read backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions for a skater to come back to the pool after a jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns POOL into LOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure-skating jump taken off from the toe pick of one skate, landing on the same edge.

clue.text: Passes an hour in church over strictly confidential matter

parts.note: to top something is to pass or surpass it, so passes gives tops

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the piece is turned upside down, read in reverse

parts.note: terce is one of the canonical hours of the church's daily office, around 9am

explanation.surface: Someone spends an hour in church brooding over a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: TERCE is the third canonical hour of prayer; 'over' reverses it to ECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly classified material, the most restricted grade of government secrecy, is top secret.

clue.text: Global production in the red — it's simply made up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, in reverse

explanation.surface: An accountant explains that worldwide losses were simply invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Global production in the red' sounds like a company losing money; it describes the ball-shaped Dutch cheese in red wax. 'made up' reverses MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dutch cheese is made in a ball shape and sold coated in red wax.

clue.text: Open forbidden ways to get in

parts.note: out means not allowed, as in 'that's out'
doors are the entrances to a building

explanation.surface: Banned entrances are being thrown open.
explanation.definitionFit: In the open air, outside rather than in a building, is out of doors.

clue.text: Took off trimmed international cricket match in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle means one piece sits within the centre of the other

parts.note: pared means trimmed or shaved down
ODI is a one-day international, a limited-overs cricket match between countries

explanation.surface: A shortened international cricket match was halted partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' suggests removal; here it means mimicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, the same as mocking them by exaggerated imitation.

clue.text: Deplete noise, including raffia curtains

indicators.note: including means the noise word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: curtains hang at the edges, so only the outer letters of raffia are taken

explanation.surface: Raffia curtains are supposed to deaden the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain resources is to use them up, exhausting or using up their supply.

clue.text: Daub number plates (not first three letters) to confuse followers

indicators.note: to confuse things is to jumble them, so the remaining letters are rearranged
this instruction removes the opening three letters of the word number

explanation.surface: Smearing number plates so that pursuers cannot read them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first three letters' strips NUM, leaving BER, which joins PLATES under 'to confuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To plaster something thickly all over is to smear or coat it messily.

clue.text: Criminal acts at house in the middle of Trieste

parts.note: a villa is a large house, typically in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: the middle of takes the central letters of Trieste

explanation.surface: Crimes committed at a house in central Trieste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' takes the central three letters of TRIESTE, IES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked deeds of villains, acts of villainy, are crimes in the plural form.

clue.text: 4 down to get high-level protection for leader of the Greens

definitions.meaning: a head covering shields the top of the body
with 4 down before it this names the outlaw who led the merry men in Lincoln green

explanation.surface: A Green Party leader seeks robust security cover.
explanation.walkthrough: '4 down to get' means put ROBIN in front: Robin Hood led outlaws dressed in Lincoln green, not the Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A head covering protects the top of the head; Robin Hood led the green-clad outlaws of Sherwood.

clue.text: 4 down to get right bloke to provide an alternative for a Guardian setter

definitions.text: an alternative for a Guardian setter

parts.note: good means right or proper
a fellow is a man, a chap or bloke

explanation.surface: A newspaper seeks the right man to cover for one of its crossword setters.
explanation.walkthrough: With ROBIN from 4 down, Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the sprite, and Puck is a Guardian crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is the folklore name of the sprite also called Puck, which is one Guardian setter's pseudonym.

clue.text: Channel divers swore a truce

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various or assorted, signalling the letters come in a different order

explanation.surface: Swimmers crossing the English Channel agreed to stop fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like underwater swimmers; it is the old adjective meaning various, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream, river or artificial canal that carries water is a water channel.

clue.text: Previous family residence used for play

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun: a structure used for play

parts.note: a family tree shows one's forebears, the previous generations
a house is a residence

explanation.surface: An ancestral home is now just a children's playroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previous family' is the family tree of ancestors, not former relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden den built in the branches is a children's play hideout.

clue.text: London Eye can be a Christmas treat

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, the slang of Londoners, the phrase rhyming with eye stands for eye
a small pastry tart filled with dried fruit, eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: Visiting the big Ferris wheel on the Thames could be a festive outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London Eye' is the Thames-side Ferris wheel, but here it means an eye in London (Cockney rhyming) slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns eye into this phrase; it is also the small fruit-filled pastry eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Never return to issue concerning former volunteers

indicators.note: return means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue or send out
on means about or concerning
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force, since renamed the Army Reserve

explanation.surface: Ex-reservists vow they will never go back to the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses EMIT, ON and TA all together.
explanation.definitionFit: On no occasion whatever, an emphatic synonym for never.

clue.text: Reserved opening avoided non-starter

parts.note: an intro is the opening of a song or piece

indicators.note: non-starter means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: averted means turned aside or avoided

explanation.surface: An opening was dodged by a horse that never ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-starter' looks like a failed idea; it drops the A of AVERTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy, inward-looking person is reserved, quiet and turned in on themselves.

clue.text: Harry has first signs of St Louis encephalitis

indicators.note: first signs takes the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A man named Harry shows early symptoms of a mosquito-borne brain disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name; it is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester or harass them persistently.

clue.text: A leading director puts on extras

indicators.note: leading takes the first letter of director

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A top film director stages a production with extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extras' looks like film crowd players; it means optional additions.
explanation.definitionFit: Optional additional items or features bolted on to a basic product.

clue.text: 4 down to get firm endorsement for a foreign secretary

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
an OK is approval or endorsement

explanation.surface: A company backs a candidate for Foreign Secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: With ROBIN from 4 down: Robin Cook was UK Foreign Secretary from 1997 to 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Cook held the post of British Foreign Secretary under Tony Blair.

clue.text: Plastic explosive applied to vehicle close to hand

parts.note: a charge is a quantity of explosive
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: close to here means the end, the last letter, of hand

explanation.surface: Plastic explosive is attached to a car within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic explosive' looks like one phrase; 'Plastic' alone is slang for credit cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is informal for credit cards and similar cards used to pay.

clue.text: Top family has many branches

definitions.meaning: the monarch's family, the highest family in the land
a stag with antlers of twelve or more points is given this name

explanation.surface: A grand family with a sprawling family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a stag whose antlers branch into twelve or more points.
explanation.definitionFit: The king's family is the top family; a stag with many-branched antlers is a deer of that name.

clue.text: A small number in Italy use a footstool regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A few people in Italy routinely rest their feet on a stool.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for eight, a smallish whole number.

clue.text: Regulation involving use of arms to target revenue

parts.note: to point at something is to aim at or target it
a duty is a tax, a source of government revenue

explanation.surface: A rule on weapons is used to aim at raising tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use of arms' suggests weapons; it is a traffic officer's signalling arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer stationed at a junction controls traffic flow by arm signals.

clue.text: Girl gets unrestricted job employed by ranchers

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun: a tool employed by ranchers

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

indicators.note: unrestricted means stripped of its outer limits, so only the middle letter of job remains

explanation.surface: A young woman lands a free-and-easy job on a cattle ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose, thrown to catch cattle on a ranch.

clue.text: I looked at what is said to be an unattractive feature

indicators.note: what is said signals the answer is pronounced like the words supplied

parts.note: I looked at means I saw

explanation.surface: Someone recalls looking at something reportedly ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'I saw' and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or object that spoils the view is an unattractive blot.

clue.text: Long way off being seen in smaller sized briefs

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for long, as in longitude or on clothing labels

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters of way are rearranged
being seen in says the letters wanted are visible within the words smaller sized, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: Long underpants look odd squeezed into a smaller size of briefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WAY to AWY, and 'being seen in' picks ERS out of smallER Sized. 'briefs' looks like underwear; it means barristers' clients' cases, and so the barristers themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs is informal for barristers or solicitors, the legal professionals who are given a brief.
